## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

*Dutiyakāyappacālaka* ("16. Swaying the body") is the sixteenth training rule in the *Sekhiya* section of the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* within the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. The rule regulates monastic decorum regarding bodily conduct, specifically prohibiting unmindful swaying or swinging of the body. An English translation of the rule and its word commentary has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

The rule is widely attested across early Buddhist monastic codes. Within the Pali tradition, direct counterparts are found in the *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* (Sk 16), the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (Sk 16), the *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (Sk 16), and the corresponding sections of both the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī *Parivāra*. Parallels outside the Theravāda lineage are preserved in Chinese and Sanskrit across several vinaya recensions, including the Sarvāstivāda, Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, and Mūlasarvāstivāda traditions.
